page: Microsoft Azure M48pds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the 64-bit ARM architecture. Managed under Microsoft Hyper-V, the server provides 48 dedicated vCPUs matched with 768.0 GB of memory, resulting in an allocation ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware setup includes 2832 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage disks. It does not include hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

The dense 1:16 vCPU-to-memory ratio targets environments constrained heavily by RAM availability rather than raw compute cycles alone. The included 2832 GB NVMe SSD volume provides fast local temporary caching and high-throughput scratch space, while the dedicated ARM vCPUs deliver continuous execution without compute-share throttling. Users should verify software compatibility for arm64 execution environments before deployment.

Given its massive memory footprint paired with dedicated ARM processing, the M48pds_v4 offers strong resource density for organizations running arm64-compatible architectures. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of x86-specific instruction sets such as AVX or AMX, alongside zero attached public IPv4 addresses out of the box.

This server type is engineered for heavy memory-bound workloads, including large-scale in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, intensive caching tiers, enterprise resource planning deployments, and extensive data transformation pipelines.
